items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: my parents took me to see him and he was very kind and let me sit by the piano... I went with Teddy Wilson and I got autographs.

ctx.x: Right. And John Thompson, “A Day in Bermuda” or whatever they called it. “A snowy Bird” you know, and learned all that stuff. And then, on this Benny Goodman record I listened to it and I looked at all the names and then in my local newspaper, the Bergen Evening Record I saw, I was about, I don’t know, 13 or 14, and it said, “Sundays at the Colonial Post on Main Street in Hackensack, New Jersey, Sundays maybe 5 PM to 8 PM Teddy Wilson.” And I said this cannot be the Teddy Wilson who’s on the Benny Goodman record…

to be a jazz musician and he’s going to be hanging out with these people with all the prejudices about, forget race for a moment, just about how jazz musicians are. I mean my parents were just normal, when I say normal people what I mean is they didn’t know anything about show biz or musicians.
